content.text: Maps are often treated as objective records, even {{gap:1}} they reflect choices made by their creators. The symbols {{gap:2}} appear on a map depend on what the map is intended to show. A transport map, for example, may omit streets {{gap:3}} are irrelevant to commuters. This does not make the map inaccurate; {{gap:4}}, it makes the information easier to use. Readers should therefore ask {{gap:5}} purpose a map serves before deciding {{gap:6}} to trust it. Only {{gap:7}} they understand its limits can they interpret it properly, rather {{gap:8}} assuming that every detail has been included.

questions.explanation: Though introduces a contrast between apparent objectivity and editorial choice.
That introduces the relative clause describing the symbols.
What purpose forms an embedded question.
Whether introduces the alternative question of trust.
Once means after the condition has been met.
Rather than introduces the rejected alternative.
